You are working in an isolated git worktree of the DeepSeek Harness monorepo. FIRST run `git log --oneline -1`; if your worktree is older than commit `4c693ee2f` on `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, run `git merge --ff-only 4c693ee2f`, then `pnpm install --offline`. Commit as soon as the gates pass; a container restart loses uncommitted work. Two other agents are concurrently changing `packages/improvement/environment-runner`, `fleet`, `shifts`, `scorekeeper`, `observatory` (one of them adds the same delegation idea to the environment runner) and `packages/subagent/**` (the other); do NOT touch those packages, `packages/governance/**`, or the Village note; read them only. You own `packages/improvement/program/**`, its fixtures, and its docs.

Read CLAUDE.md, packages/AGENTS.md, examples/AGENTS.md, docs/AGENTS.md, docs/testing.md, `.agents/notes/README.md`, and follow every convention (everything is a plugin; per-file 100% coverage; bilingual triplets; model-visible ⟺ logged; explicit `resolve` defaulting; misconfiguration fails loud; enforce a decision in the operation that makes it; a non-trivial change carries an Agent Note in the same commit).

## Task: program departments delegated to an external coding agent

`packages/improvement/program` (`ctx.program`, read `src/index.ts`, `spec.ts`, `ledger.ts`, `types.ts`, the tests, the README, and the program-ledger note `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-program-ledger.*`) runs one department per goal: a harness agent in its own git worktree, driven through the LLM seam (`installModelSelection`, turns, the one follow-up user turn when checks fail), then integration merge, release, and signoff gates. This slice adds a second way to staff a department: delegating the goal to an out-of-process coding agent through the subagent seam (`packages/subagent/subagent`: `ctx.subagents.start(name, { prompt, parent, signal, label? })`; providers `claude-code`, `codex`, `acp`, `dsh-sdk`, plus the in-process `fork`/`spawn` providers that inherit the parent's route, which the mock route serves keylessly; read their READMEs and how each derives the child cwd from the parent agent's session), while the program keeps everything it owns: the ledger events, the worktree, the budget caps, the checks it runs, the department's certification, integration, release, and signoff.

Design, mirroring the runner slice so the two read alike (do not import from the runner; keep the few lines of validation local to the program):

1. `ProgramSpec.implementer?: { kind: 'route' } | { kind: 'subagent', provider: string, label?: string }`, defaulted to `{ kind: 'route' }` in the spec's explicit resolve step, included in the program digest (a digest change is intended: a program staffed differently is a different program), and validated when a department starts: `PROGRAM_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE` naming the provider when `ctx.subagents` is absent or has no such provider; refused for a deployment `isolation` above `none` when the provider is out-of-process (an in-process provider inherits the composition and may keep the deployment's isolation), with a pinned error code.
2. For `kind: 'subagent'` the department still gets its session, worktree, stamp, caps, and `agent/session-start` as today, but instead of driving turns the program starts one child run per attempt through `ctx.subagents.start(provider, { prompt: [the goal text on the first attempt, the existing check-failure turn text on later ones], parent: departmentAgent, signal, label })` in the department worktree (set the department agent's cwd so the provider derives it; if a provider needs an explicit cwd, pass it as its README documents), awaits the result, appends a durable `program/delegation { goalKey, attempt, provider, runId, stopReason, structured?, usage? }` event to the department session (declared in `src/types.ts` by `SessionEventMap` merging, persistence catalog regenerated), and then runs the department's checks and certification exactly as today; the round cap bounds attempts as it bounds turns. Reconciliation after a restart reads the delegation events like any other department state and never re-runs a delegated attempt that ended.
3. The ledger's `program/start` (or the event that records the spec) carries `implementer` durably, and the README states what a delegated department's certificate proves (the program ran the checks on the tree the external agent left in the worktree) and what it does not (no model-visible history of the implementer lives in our log; the department's trajectory carries no steps).
4. **Tests**: unit specs at 100% per-file coverage over a stubbed subagent service (delegation per attempt, follow-up prompt carrying the check-failure text, the durable event, refusal without the provider, refusal above `none` for out-of-process, the route default, reconciliation after an ended delegation); a Loader-booted keyless e2e under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program-external-implementer/` using the in-process provider that inherits the parent route over the mock route (whichever the existing program e2e's route mock supports), proving a delegated department certifies on a goal the mock can satisfy, and that a failing goal records one delegation event per attempt up to the round cap; plus `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program-claude-implementer/cordis.yml` composing `subagent-claude-code` as the provider with the program, budget policy, persistence, checkpoint policy, signoff, and a driver that runs a one-goal program ("add a `hello.txt` containing `hello` at the worktree root" with a check that reads it) with `implementer: { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'claude-code' }`; its e2e is a with-key style test that self-skips unless `DSH_E2E_CLAUDE_CODE=1` (docstring: drives the real Claude Code CLI on the host's own authentication, run by hand). Do not run the real Claude Code e2e unless `claude -p "ok"` works in your worktree shell; if it does, run it once and report the result.
5. **Docs**: README pair (the two implementer kinds, the certificate statement, the isolation rule, the digest consequence), `docs/subsystems/improvement.md` program section (+ ZH, type-equiv in sync), catalogs regenerated (`gen-cordis-catalog`, `gen-config-catalog`, `gen-doc-graphs`, `gen-persistence-catalog`) with Chinese twins mirrored and pairing re-recorded, `verify-village-composition` unchanged (program compositions already count as district compositions), a bilingual Agent Note `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-program-external-implementer.md` (+ `.zh.md`) written first with the required sections.

Gates before committing, all must pass: `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `vitest run --coverage --coverage.include 'packages/improvement/program/src/**'`, `vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts packages/improvement/program`, `pnpm run test:snapshot -t "program"`, `pnpm run verify-village-composition`, `pnpm run verify-cordis-config`, `pnpm run verify-package-invariants`, `pnpm run rescope-vendor:check` (after `git add` of every new file), `pnpm run knip`, `pnpm run duplication`, `pnpm run doc-sync`.

Constraints: never commit credentials; `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is absent. Put no model name or identifier in code, docs, fixtures, or the commit message (the provider id `claude-code` is the existing package's name and is fine). Commit on your worktree branch with the message `feat(program): departments delegated to external coding agents under the program's own certificates` ending with these two trailer lines exactly:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C

Report back: the commit sha and branch, the spec field and event as implemented, which in-process provider the keyless e2e uses, whether the real Claude Code program ran and its outcome, every deviation, the gate commands with results, and anything you could not do.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- dsh-archive-agent-notes: Use when adding, auditing, pruning, archiving, restoring, or reviewing Agent Notes in deepseek-harness; checks every new note for superseded active records, classifies implemented notes by future decision value, deletes rejected notes that no longer prevent a tempting fallacy, and applies the frozen archived/{kind} triplet and manifest rules.
- dsh-code-review: Use when reviewing a pull request in the deepseek-harness repo — orients the reviewer to this codebase's standards (AGENTS.md conventions, defensive patterns, ADRs, quality gates) and the review-specific checks that code alone can't show
- dsh-doc-site-sync: Use when publishing, updating, moving, or removing DeepSeek Harness documentation website pages; editing website/docs.ts mappings or navigation; diagnosing a page missing from the VitePress site; fixing projected documentation links; or running the docs:dev, docs:check, and doc-sync workflow after website-content changes.
- dsh-doc-standards: Use when writing, moving, reviewing, or auditing documentation in the deepseek-harness repo — choosing hierarchy and detail, separating tutorials from references, checking tutorial progression, trimming doc slop, responding to a verify-doc-budgets failure, or requests like "improve the docs", "audit the docs", "where should this be documented", or "this doc is too long".
- dsh-find-simplifications: Use when working in the deepseek-harness repo to find non-obvious simplification candidates, write proposed Agent Notes or inline TODO/FIXME/XXX notes, audit or coalesce superseded Agent Notes, or fold worthwhile simplification ideas from another PR; especially for dead, duplicated, speculative, over-built, added-then-removed, or hand-rolled-where-a-dependency-exists surfaces.
- dsh-merging-stacked-prs: Use when landing a stack of dependent GitHub PRs (A ← B ← C, where each bases on the one below) onto master, merging a PR whose base is another open PR's branch, or whenever a request mentions "stacked PRs", "PR stack", "dependent PRs", or merging several related PRs in sequence. Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.
- dsh-pre-push-checks: Use before pushing, force-pushing, marking ready for review, or claiming checks pass on a deepseek-harness branch, and immediately after gh stack sync publishes rewritten branches, to select the smallest tests and checks that cover the outgoing or just-published diff without reflexively running the full repository suite.
- dsh-prose-standard: Use when writing, reviewing, restoring, trimming, or auditing prose in the deepseek-harness repo, including deciding where documentation or comments are required across Markdown, JSDoc, code and test comments, prompts, descriptions, diagnostics, and CLI or UI strings.
- dsh-trim-cot-leakage: Use when auditing or fixing prose that reads like a leaked reasoning transcript — dead design-session citations such as (decision N), audit item codes, or §N of uncommitted drafts; change narration such as "used to", "no longer", "this cut"; stack or review vantage ("a later PR in this stack", "rejected in review"); reviewer-addressed justifications; control-flow narration; or hedged planning residue in comments, JSDoc, docs, or Agent Notes.
- record-browser-gif: Record browser or Web UI interaction demos as optimized GIFs using the available built-in browser, state-based frame capture, and deterministic encoding, then publish to a dedicated assets branch when the task includes attaching the GIF to a pull request. Use when asked to make, record, or generate a GIF that demonstrates a browser workflow, and for every pull request that changes product-user-visible GUI behavior, which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and model flow.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). # AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own build transcripts (see data/transcripts/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,

  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few

172	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
173	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
174	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
175	}

177	/** Keep the tail of longer text inside the bound, marking what was dropped. */
178	function bounded(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
179	  return text.length <= maxChars ? text : `…${text.slice(text.length - maxChars + 1)}`
180	}
181	
182	/** Render one executed command's outcome: the exit fact, then whatever it wrote. */
183	function outcomeOf(result: ShellRunResult): string {
184	  const exit = result.exitCode === null
185	    ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}`
186	    : `exit ${String(result.exitCode)}`
187	  const written = [result.stdout.text, result.stderr.text]
188	    .map(stream => stream.trim())
189	    .filter(stream => stream !== '')
190	    .join('\n')
191	  return written === '' ? exit : `${exit}\n${written}`
192	}

194	/** The one user turn a department receives when its checks did not pass. */
195	function retryText(failures: readonly CheckResult[]): string {
196	  const listed = failures.map(failure => `- ${failure.checkId}: ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n')
197	  return `<checks_failed>\n${String(failures.length)} of this goal's checks did not pass on the branch as it stands.\n${listed}\nKeep working and commit; the checks run again when you stop.\n</checks_failed>`

254	  /**
255	   * Start one program, or resume the program its spec already identifies.
256	   *
257	   * The spec is frozen into a digest before anything runs, so starting the same
258	   * spec twice addresses one program: the second call reconciles the existing
259	   * ledger instead of forking a second one.
260	   * @param spec - the deliverable to run.
261	   * @returns the ledger this pass left behind.
262	   * @throws {@link ProgramError} when the spec, its presets, or the spec-freeze
263	   *   signature the program session must carry cannot support a program.
264	   */
265	  async start(spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<ProgramReport> {
266	    const frozen = resolveProgramSpec(spec)
267	    if (!PROGRAM_REVISION.test(frozen.baseRevision)) {
268	      throw new ProgramError(`baseRevision "${frozen.baseRevision}" is not a revision the composed shell can carry unquoted`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
269	    }
270	    await this.requirePresets(frozen)
271	    const programId = programIdFor(programSpecDigest(frozen))
272	    return await this.enqueue(() => this.open(programId, frozen))
273	  }

275	  /**
276	   * Reconcile every unfinished program in the persistence root and carry it on.
277	   *
278	   * Each program's goals are read from their own department sessions and
279	   * worktrees rather than from the ledger, so a process that died between a
280	   * durable fact and its ledger record records the fact rather than repeating
281	   * the work.
282	   * @returns one report per program this pass reconciled, in scan order.
283	   */

309	  /**
310	   * Chain one pass onto the single work queue. The queue itself is always the
311	   * caught form, so a pass that rejects delays the next one instead of
312	   * poisoning the chain.

314	  private async enqueue<T>(pass: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
315	    const next = this.queue.then(() => pass())
316	    this.queue = next.catch(() => {

318	      // delivered to the caller through `next`.

340	  /** Read every persisted session once: the program ledgers and the member stamps. */
341	  private async scan(): Promise<{ ledgers: ProgramLedger[]; members: ProgramMemberSpend[]; sessions: Map<SessionId, ScannedSession> }> {
342	    const ledgers: ProgramLedger[] = []
343	    const members: ProgramMemberSpend[] = []
344	    const sessions = new Map<SessionId, ScannedSession>()
345	    for (const header of await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()) {
346	      const inspection = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(header.id)
347	      const scanned: ScannedSession = { meta: inspection.meta, events: inspection.events }
348	      sessions.set(header.id, scanned)

351	      const member = memberSpend(scanned, foldBudgetSpend(inspection.events, {}).totalTokens)

354	    return { ledgers, members, sessions }

357	  /** Reconcile and carry on every program whose ledger has no closing record. */
358	  private async reconcileAll(): Promise<ProgramReport[]> {
359	    const scan = await this.scan()
360	    const reports: ProgramReport[] = []
361	    for (const ledger of scan.ledgers) {
362	      if (this.stopping) break
363	      if (ledger.end !== undefined) continue
364	      reports.push(await this.pickUp(ledger, scan.sessions))

369	  /** Start a program that has no ledger yet, or reconcile the one it already has. */
370	  private async open(programId: ProgramId, spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<ProgramReport> {
371	    const scan = await this.scan()
372	    const existing = scan.ledgers.find(ledger => ledger.start.programId === programId)
373	    if (existing !== undefined) {
374	      if (existing.end !== undefined) return this.finishedReport(existing)
375	      return await this.pickUp(existing, scan.sessions)
376	    }
377	    const sessionId = SessionId(programId)
378	    const carried = scan.sessions.get(sessionId)
379	    this.requireSignoffRecord(spec, carried?.events ?? [], 'spec-freeze', 'start')
380	    if (carried === undefined) {
381	      const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(sessionId, { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
382	      return await this.publish(session, () => this.begin(session, programId, spec))
383	    }
384	    // The program id is derived from the spec digest, so a caller signing the
385	    // spec freeze addresses this session before the program exists. Its log is
386	    // continued rather than replaced, or the signature it holds would be lost.
387	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(sessionId)
388	    try {
389	      return await this.publish(preparation.session, () => this.begin(preparation.session, programId, spec))
390	    } finally {
391	      preparation[Symbol.dispose]()
392	    }
393	  }

395	  /** Declare the program and every goal of its spec, then run it. */
396	  private async begin(session: Session, programId: ProgramId, spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<ProgramReport> {
397	    session.append('program/start', {
398	      programId,
399	      specSha256: programSpecDigest(spec),
400	      spec,
401	      baseRevision: spec.baseRevision,
402	      ...spec.signoff === undefined ? {} : { signoff: spec.signoff },
403	    })
404	    const run = this.newRun(programId, spec, session)
405	    for (const state of run.states.values()) this.record(run, state)
406	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
407	    return await this.drive(run)
408	  }

410	  /**
411	   * Reject a transition this deployment gates on a signature the program
412	   * session does not carry, or carries over another artefact than the spec
413	   * names. The signature is a `signoff/recorded` a caller appended through
414	   * `ctx.signoffs`; this service reads it and never writes one.
415	   * @param spec - the frozen spec, whose `signoff` names the attested artefact.
416	   * @param events - the program session's events, oldest first.
417	   * @param transition - the signature the transition needs.
418	   * @param transitioning - the refused transition, for the message.
419	   */
420	  private requireSignoffRecord(
421	    spec: ProgramSpec,
422	    events: readonly SessionEvent[],
423	    transition: SignoffTransition,
424	    transitioning: string,
425	  ): void {
426	    if (!this.config.requireSignoff) return
427	    const artefact = spec.signoff?.artefactSha256
428	    if (artefact === undefined) {
429	      throw new ProgramError(
430	        `this deployment requires a signoff record before a program may ${transitioning}, and the spec names no artefact for one to attest`,
431	        'PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED',
432	      )
433	    }
434	    const record = latestSignoff(events, transition)
435	    if (record === undefined) {
436	      throw new ProgramError(
437	        `this deployment requires a "${transition}" signoff/recorded on the program session before a program may ${transitioning}`,
438	        'PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED',
439	      )
440	    }
441	    if (record.artefactSha256 !== artefact) {
442	      throw new ProgramError(
443	        `the "${transition}" signoff/recorded attests artefact ${record.artefactSha256}, which is not the spec's ${artefact}`,
444	        'PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED',
445	      )
446	    }
447	  }

449	  /** Reconcile one existing program from its departments and carry it on. */
450	  private async pickUp(ledger: ProgramLedger, sessions: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, ScannedSession>): Promise<ProgramReport> {
451	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(ledger.sessionId)
452	    try {
453	      return await this.publish(preparation.session, async () => {
454	        const run = this.newRun(ledger.start.programId, ledger.start.spec, preparation.session)
455	        run.integration = ledger.integration
456	        for (const state of run.states.values()) {
457	          const recorded = ledger.goals.get(state.goal.key)
458	          if (recorded !== undefined) {
459	            state.status = recorded.status
460	            state.sessionId = recorded.sessionId
461	            state.workspace = recorded.workspace
462	            state.revision = recorded.revision
463	            state.reason = recorded.reason
464	          }
465	          const reconciled = await this.reconcile(run, state, sessions)
466	          // A goal the ledger never recorded is declared here as well, so a
467	          // ledger written by a process that died mid-declaration still states
468	          // every goal of the spec before it states what became of any of them.
469	          if (recorded === undefined || reconciled) this.record(run, state)
470	        }
471	        preparation.session.append('program/resume', {
472	          programId: run.programId,
473	          statuses: countStatuses([...run.states.values()].map(state => state.status)),
474	        })
475	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(preparation.session)
476	        return await this.drive(run)
477	      })
478	    } finally {
479	      preparation[Symbol.dispose]()
480	    }
481	  }

484	  private newRun(programId: ProgramId, spec: ProgramSpec, session: Session): ProgramRun {
485	    return {
486	      programId,
487	      spec,
488	      session,
489	      states: new Map(spec.goals.map(goal => [goal.key, {
490	        goal,
491	        status: 'pending',
492	        sessionId: undefined,
493	        workspace: undefined,
494	        revision: undefined,
495	        reason: undefined,
496	        driving: false,
497	      }])),
498	      integration: undefined,

503	  /**
504	   * Bring one goal's state in line with what its department states about
505	   * itself. The department's own log and worktree are the authority; the ledger
506	   * record this pass read is only the index that found them.
507	   * @returns whether the reconciled status differs from the recorded one.
508	   */
509	  private async reconcile(
510	    run: ProgramRun,
511	    state: DepartmentState,
512	    sessions: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, ScannedSession>,
513	  ): Promise<boolean> {
514	    const before = state.status
515	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, state.goal.key)
516	    const scanned = sessions.get(sessionId)
517	    if (scanned === undefined) {
518	      state.status = 'pending'
519	      return before !== state.status
520	    }
521	    state.sessionId = sessionId
522	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, state.goal.key)
523	    state.workspace = workspace
524	    if (!await isDirectory(workspace)) {
525	      state.status = 'failed'
526	      state.reason = `the worktree at ${workspace} is gone, so nothing can show what this department delivered`
527	      return true
528	    }
529	    const department = foldDepartmentLog(scanned.events)
530	    if (department.certified) {
531	      state.status = 'certified'
532	      state.revision = await this.head(workspace)
533	      return before !== state.status
534	    }
535	    if (department.phase === 'blocked') {
536	      state.status = 'blocked'
537	      state.reason = department.blockedCode
538	      return before !== state.status
539	    }
540	    state.status = 'running'
541	    return before !== state.status
542	  }

559	    state.status = status

565	  /** Run departments until none can start, then integrate or close the program. */
566	  private async drive(run: ProgramRun): Promise<ProgramReport> {
567	    const running = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
568	    let ceilingReached = false
569	    while (!this.stopping) {
570	      const runnable = [...run.states.values()].filter(state => !state.driving && this.canRun(run, state))
571	      for (const state of runnable) {
572	        if (running.size >= this.config.maxConcurrentGoals) break
573	        if (await this.overCeiling(run)) {
574	          ceilingReached = true
575	          break
576	        }
577	        state.driving = true
578	        running.set(state.goal.key, this.department(run, state).finally(() => {
579	          state.driving = false
580	          running.delete(state.goal.key)
581	        }))
582	      }
583	      if (running.size === 0) break
584	      await Promise.race(running.values())
585	    }
586	    await Promise.all(running.values())
587	    if (this.stopping) return this.report(run)
588	    return await this.close(run, ceilingReached)
589	  }

591	  /** Whether one goal is ready for a department pass right now. */
592	  private canRun(run: ProgramRun, state: DepartmentState): boolean {
593	    if (state.status === 'running') return true
594	    if (state.status !== 'pending') return false
595	    return state.goal.dependsOn.every((key) => {
596	      const dependency = run.states.get(key)
597	      return dependency?.status === 'certified' || dependency?.status === 'merged'
598	    })
599	  }

601	  /** Whether the program's own sessions already spent its ceiling. */
602	  private async overCeiling(run: ProgramRun): Promise<boolean> {
603	    const ceiling = run.spec.tokenCeiling
604	    if (ceiling === undefined) return false
605	    const { members } = await this.scan()
606	    return programSpend(members, run.programId) >= ceiling
607	  }

609	  /** Integrate a fully certified program, or close one that cannot reach that. */
610	  private async close(run: ProgramRun, ceilingReached: boolean): Promise<ProgramReport> {
611	    const states = [...run.states.values()]
612	    if (states.every(state => state.status === 'certified')) {
613	      // A process that died between the integration's certificate and the
614	      // records that follow it finishes the bookkeeping instead of merging
615	      // the same branches a second time.
616	      if (run.integration?.status === 'certified') await this.markMerged(run)
617	      else await this.integrate(run)
618	    }
619	    if (states.every(state => state.status === 'merged')) return await this.release(run)
620	    for (const state of states) {
621	      if (state.status === 'pending') await this.transition(run, state, 'abandoned', 'the program ended before this goal started')
622	    }
623	    run.outcome = ceilingReached ? 'abandoned' : 'failed'
624	    run.session.append('program/end', { programId: run.programId, outcome: run.outcome })
625	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
626	    return this.report(run)
627	  }

629	  /** Record the release of a program whose integration certified its merged head. */
630	  private async release(run: ProgramRun): Promise<ProgramReport> {
631	    this.requireSignoffRecord(run.spec, run.session.events, 'release', 'release')
632	    const mergedRevision = run.integration?.mergedRevision
633	    run.outcome = 'released'
634	    run.session.append('program/end', {
635	      programId: run.programId,
636	      outcome: 'released',
637	      ...mergedRevision === undefined ? {} : { mergedRevision },
638	    })
639	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
640	    return this.report(run)
641	  }

643	  /** Merge every department branch onto the base revision and certify the result. */
644	  private async integrate(run: ProgramRun): Promise<void> {
645	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
646	    const branch = this.branchName(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
647	    try {
648	      await this.ensureWorktree(workspace, branch, run.spec.baseRevision)
649	    } catch (error: unknown) {
650	      await this.failIntegration(run, String(error))
651	      return
652	    }
653	    run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'running' }
654	    run.session.append('program/integration', run.integration)
655	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
656	    try {
657	      for (const key of dependencyOrder(run.spec.goals)) {
658	        const departmentBranch = this.branchName(run.programId, key)
659	        await this.git(['merge', '--no-ff', '-m', departmentBranch, departmentBranch], workspace)
660	      }
661	    } catch (error: unknown) {
662	      await this.failIntegration(run, String(error))
663	      return
664	    }
665	    const certified = await this.driveIntegration(run, workspace)
666	    if (certified) await this.markMerged(run)
667	  }

670	  private async markMerged(run: ProgramRun): Promise<void> {
671	    for (const state of run.states.values()) await this.transition(run, state, 'merged', undefined)

675	  private async failIntegration(run: ProgramRun, reason: string): Promise<void> {
676	    run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'failed', reason }

681	  /** Certify the merged head, letting a model fix it when the checks do not pass as merged. */
682	  private async driveIntegration(run: ProgramRun, workspace: string): Promise<boolean> {
683	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
684	    const handle = await this.createSession(sessionId, workspace, undefined, run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
685	    try {
686	      const { agent } = handle
687	      const goal = this.ctx.goals.create(agent, {
688	        objective: `Make the merged head of "${run.spec.objective}" pass its integration standard.`,
689	        maxGoalRounds: this.config.maxGoalRounds,
690	      })
691	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
692	      this.ctx.completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: integrationChecks(run.spec.integration) })
693	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
694	      // The merge itself is the first candidate: a clean merge whose checks
695	      // pass needs no model turn at all.
696	      const certified = await this.attempts(agent, workspace, 'none', undefined)
697	      if (!certified) {
698	        await this.failIntegration(run, 'the merged head did not pass the integration standard')
699	        return false
700	      }
701	      const mergedRevision = await this.head(workspace)
702	      run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'certified', mergedRevision, sessionId }
703	      run.session.append('program/integration', run.integration)
704	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
705	      return true
706	    } finally {
707	      await handle.dispose()
708	    }
709	  }

711	  /** Create or resume one department, drive it, and record what it came to. */
712	  private async department(run: ProgramRun, state: DepartmentState): Promise<void> {
713	    const { goal } = state
714	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, goal.key)
715	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, goal.key)
716	    const resuming = state.status === 'running'
717	    let handle: AgentHandle
718	    try {
719	      handle = resuming
720	        ? await this.resumeSession(sessionId, goal.preset)
721	        : await this.openDepartment(run, state, workspace, sessionId)
722	    } catch (error: unknown) {
723	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', String(error))
724	      return
725	    }
726	    try {
727	      await this.driveDepartment(run, state, handle.agent, workspace, resuming)
728	    } catch (error: unknown) {
729	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', String(error))
730	    } finally {
731	      await handle.dispose()
732	    }
733	  }

735	  /** Mint one department's worktree and session, then record it as running. */
736	  private async openDepartment(
737	    run: ProgramRun,
738	    state: DepartmentState,
739	    workspace: string,
740	    sessionId: SessionId,
741	  ): Promise<AgentHandle> {
742	    const { goal } = state
743	    await this.ensureWorktree(workspace, this.branchName(run.programId, goal.key), run.spec.baseRevision)
744	    const handle = await this.createSession(sessionId, workspace, goal.preset, run.programId, goal.key)
745	    const { agent } = handle
746	    try {
747	      agent.session.append('budget/caps', goal.budget)
748	      const created = this.ctx.goals.create(agent, { objective: goal.objective, maxGoalRounds: this.config.maxGoalRounds })
749	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
750	      this.ctx.completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: created.id, checks: goal.checks })
751	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
752	    } catch (error: unknown) {
753	      await handle.dispose()
754	      throw error
755	    }
756	    state.sessionId = sessionId
757	    state.workspace = workspace
758	    await this.transition(run, state, 'running', undefined)
759	    return handle
760	  }

762	  /** Drive one department's attempts until it certifies, blocks, or runs out of rounds. */
763	  private async driveDepartment(
764	    run: ProgramRun,
765	    state: DepartmentState,
766	    agent: Agent,
767	    workspace: string,
768	    resuming: boolean,
769	  ): Promise<void> {
770	    // A department whose goal is blocked is never driven: the reconciliation
771	    // routes it to `blocked` and waits for an operator's own resume.
772	    const current = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
773	    if (current === undefined) {
774	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', 'the department session carries no goal')
775	      return
776	    }
777	    if (resuming) {
778	      // A department loaded from persistence starts disarmed; the resume edge
779	      // is the durable record that this process took it back over, and the
780	      // disarm that follows keeps the attempts this service's rather than the
781	      // goal-round driver's. A goal the previous process completed without a
782	      // certificate cannot be resumed, and fails the department loudly.
783	      this.ctx.goals.resume(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
784	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
785	    }
786	    const certified = await this.attempts(agent, workspace, state.goal.isolation, state.goal.objective)
787	    const settled = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
788	    if (settled?.phase === 'blocked') {
789	      await this.transition(run, state, 'blocked', settled.blockedReason?.code)
790	      return
791	    }
792	    if (!certified) {
793	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', `no certificate after ${String(this.config.maxGoalRounds)} rounds`)
794	      return
795	    }
796	    state.revision = await this.head(workspace)
797	    await this.transition(run, state, 'certified', undefined)
798	  }

800	  /**
801	   * Run the session's standard against its workspace, letting the model work
802	   * between attempts, until it certifies or the round cap is spent.
803	   * @param agent - the session being certified.
804	   * @param workspace - the worktree the checks execute in.
805	   * @param isolation - the isolation level the certified run claims.
806	   * @param objective - the first user turn, or `undefined` to measure before any turn.
807	   * @returns whether a run certified the standard.
808	   */
809	  private async attempts(
810	    agent: Agent,
811	    workspace: string,
812	    isolation: CertificateIsolation,
813	    objective: string | undefined,
814	  ): Promise<boolean> {
815	    let prompt = objective
816	    for (let round = 1; round <= this.config.maxGoalRounds; round += 1) {
817	      if (prompt !== undefined) {
818	        agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
819	        await agent.whenIdle()
820	        const goal = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
821	        if (goal?.phase === 'blocked') return false
822	      }
823	      const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
824	      if (standard === undefined) return false
825	      const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
826	      const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, workspace)
827	      const outcome = this.ctx.completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, isolation, results, { executor: 'runner' })
828	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
829	      if (outcome.certified) {
830	        const goal = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
831	        if (goal !== undefined) this.ctx.goals.complete(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision })
832	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
833	        return true
834	      }
835	      this.ctx.completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, {
836	        rootCause: `${String(outcome.failures.length)} of this goal's checks did not pass`,
837	        detail: bounded(outcome.failures.map(failure => `${failure.checkId}: ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), this.config.evidenceMaxChars),
838	      })
839	      prompt = retryText(outcome.failures)
840	    }
841	    return false
842	  }

844	  /** Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the worktree. */
845	  private async execute(checks: readonly StandardCheck[], workspace: string): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
846	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
847	    for (const check of checks) {
848	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(this.ctx.shell.resolve({ command: check.run, workdir: workspace }))
849	      results.push({
850	        checkId: check.id,
851	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
852	        evidence: bounded(outcomeOf(result), this.config.evidenceMaxChars),
853	      })
854	    }
855	    return results
856	  }
